1 FACULTY SENATE OFFICE UNIVERSITY OF RHODE ISLAND FACULTY SENATE March 24, 2022 Faculty Senate Curriculum and Standards Committee Report 2021-2022-7 At the March 3, 2022 meeting of the Curriculum and Standards Committee, the following matters were considered and are now presented to the Faculty Senate.
SECTION II Curricular Matters Which Require Confirmation by the Faculty Senate PROGRAM CHANGES: COLLEGE OF BUSINESS: Bachelor of Science in Business Administration: Business Analytics and Intelligence major: In 2007, the Management Information Systems major was suspended due to low enrollment and resource constraints.
The refreshed major will be renamed Business Analytics and Intelligence and will be offered, along with the previously approved minor, to help prepare students to meet the high demand for professionals.
As companies are increasingly data-driven, there is demand for business professionals with knowledge, skills, and abilities in business analytics and artificial intelligence.
As a result, there are many job opportunities and high average starting salaries associated with positions at a wide range of organizations.

There was a strategic gift from Al Verrecchia to help develop student competencies in the Artificial Intelligence space, and the university previously reallocated resources required to offer the major again.
Bachelor of Science in Business Administration: Accounting major: The program change makes the number of credits required in the Accounting major 120 instead of 121.
A four-credit course that was required as part of the major is no longer required.
Therefore, it is possible to complete the degree requirements with 120 credits.
Bachelor of Science in Business Administration: General Business Administration major: General Business will go back to being a separate major and will no longer be a track in Management.
The program change that was made last year (where students would start coursework in fall 2023) resulted in confusion for students, faculty, and stakeholders.
The General Business major previously served over 200 majors each year, which makes it a critical offering for the College of Business and the University.

Bachelor of Science in Business Administration: Management major: The proposed program change streamlines the options in the management major and distinguishes the management major from general business.
General Business will go back to being a separate major and will no longer be a track in Management.
The program change that was made last year (where students would start coursework in fall 2023) resulted in confusion for students, faculty, and stakeholders.
Bachelor of Science in Business Administration: Innovation and Entrepreneurship major: Update and revise requirements for major and minor as well as correct catalog copy.
